hero.tagline: An impressionist journey through light, philosophy & the cosmos

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Selene's silver chariot
moon.intro: The Moon controls the tides of the ocean and the tides of the mind. In Vedic thought, Chandra governs the Manas — the emotional mind — and its phases mirror the cycles of human desire and detachment.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: Ego, arrogance & the ocean of self
philosophy.intro: Arrogance is the ego's armor. But armor is heavy — it slows the warrior. The Gita teaches that true strength comes not from the assertion of self but from the surrender to dharma.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Wisdom from the Bhagavad Gita
gita.intro: The Bhagavad Gita begins not with wisdom but with despair. Arjuna, the greatest warrior, drops his bow and says, 'I will not fight.' The scripture teaches that the darkest moment precedes the greatest clarity.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Shiva & the cosmic rhythm
shiva.intro: The Nataraja statue of Shiva dancing within a ring of fire is one of the most recognized symbols in the world. Physicist Fritjof Capra wrote that 'the dance of Shiva is the dance of subatomic matter' — modern physics and ancient mythology converging on the same truth.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Art, beauty & the act of seeing
art.intro: The sunflower turns its face to the light. In this simple act is a metaphor for the spiritual life — the constant orientation of the soul toward what illuminates, even when the source is hidden.
